meta.title: Driving Safety
meta.description: Covers pre-trip vehicle preparation, maintaining a safety cushion, distracted driving, driving in adverse conditions, sharing the road, emergency responses to hydroplaning and blowouts, and crash reporting procedures.

lessons.driving-preparation:
**Pre-Trip Preparation and Vehicle Inspection**

Safe driving begins before the vehicle moves. Drivers should inspect the vehicle before each trip, checking tires for inflation and condition, mirrors for correct adjustment, lights and signals for operation, brakes, fluid levels, and seat belt function. The driver must also be alert, rested, and unimpaired by fatigue, illness, or medication. Adjusting the seat, mirrors, and headrest before driving improves control and reduces distraction once the vehicle is in motion. Any defects that could make the vehicle unsafe must be reported and corrected before driving.
lessons.safety-cushion-following:
**Safety Cushion and Following Distance**

Maintaining a safety cushion — adequate space on all sides of the vehicle — gives drivers time to react to hazards and room to maneuver in emergencies. Larger and heavier vehicles require significantly more distance to stop than smaller vehicles traveling at the same speed. Following too closely, or tailgating, reduces reaction time and increases crash risk. If another driver is tailgating, gradually reduce speed and allow them to pass safely rather than accelerating or braking suddenly.
lessons.distracted-driving:
**Distracted Driving**

Distractions fall into three categories: visual (eyes off the road), manual (hands off the wheel), and cognitive (mind off the task of driving). Texting while driving is especially dangerous because it involves all three types of distraction simultaneously. Other common distractions include phone calls, eating, adjusting controls, and talking with passengers. Eliminating distractions before driving — including silencing phones and setting GPS destinations — is the safest approach.
lessons.adverse-conditions:
**Driving in Adverse Conditions**

Rain, fog, snow, ice, and low light require reduced speed, increased following distance, and heightened awareness. On wet roads, hydroplaning occurs when a tire loses contact with the pavement and rides on a layer of water. If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator and avoid sudden braking or sharp steering. At night, headlights limit visibility; overdriving headlights means traveling faster than the distance within which you can stop safely. Adjust speed to match conditions, not just the posted limit.
lessons.sharing-road:
**Sharing the Road**

Large trucks, buses, school buses, motorcycles, bicyclists, and pedestrians all share the roadway and require specific awareness. Large trucks have large blind spots on all four sides; avoid lingering in these zones. Pass trucks on the left when possible and only when the full length of the truck is visible in your mirrors before merging. School buses require stopping when lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended. Give all vulnerable road users extra space and expect that their movements may be unpredictable.
lessons.emergency-response-driving:
**Responding to Driving Emergencies**

Common driving emergencies include tire blowouts, brake failures, and hydroplaning. During a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly, maintain the vehicle's direction, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually without sharp braking. Do not jerk the wheel or slam the brakes. For brake failure, downshift, use the emergency brake gradually, look for a safe runoff area, and alert other drivers. Stay calm in all emergencies — sudden movements typically make the situation worse.
lessons.crash-reporting:
**Crash Reporting and Vehicle Defects**

If a crash occurs while driving a company vehicle, stay calm, check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, exchange information with other parties, and document the incident. Do not move injured persons unless there is an immediate danger. Notify your supervisor as required. For vehicle defects discovered before or during a trip, report the problem and do not operate the vehicle until it has been inspected and cleared as safe. Road rage incidents and near-misses should also be reported so patterns can be identified and addressed.

questions.questionText: Which OSHA requirement is the primary compliance anchor for workplace driving safety?

options.text: Lockout/Tagout Standard
Section 5(a)(1), General Duty Clause
Hazard Communication Standard
Respiratory Protection Standard

questions.questionText: Safe driving begins only after the vehicle is moving.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Which of the following should be checked before driving?

options.text: Tires
Mirrors
Lights
All of the above

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of maintaining a safety cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: To help you drive faster
To give you room to maneuver in an emergency
To prevent other vehicles from passing you
To reduce the need for mirrors

questions.questionText: A larger or heavier vehicle generally needs more distance to stop than a lighter vehicle traveling at the same speed.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Which type of distraction involves taking your eyes off the road?

options.text: Manual
Visual
Cognitive
Mechanical

questions.questionText: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because it can involve:

options.text: Visual distraction only
Manual distraction only
Cognitive distraction only
Visual, manual, and cognitive distraction simultaneously

questions.questionText: You are driving in heavy rain and feel the vehicle begin to hydroplane. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes immediately
Accelerate sharply to regain traction
Ease off the accelerator and avoid sudden braking or turning
Turn the wheel sharply toward the shoulder

questions.questionText: It is safe to remain beside a large truck as long as you are traveling at the speed limit.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Brake suddenly to warn them to back off
Speed up aggressively to create distance
Gradually reduce speed and allow them to pass when safe
Make eye contact and gesture for them to back off

questions.questionText: You are involved in a minor crash while driving a company vehicle and no one appears seriously injured. What should you do?

options.text: Leave if the vehicle still runs
Stay calm, check for injuries, call police if required, exchange information, document the incident, and notify your supervisor
Move injured people immediately regardless of their condition
Only report it if there is major vehicle damage

questions.questionText: What should you do if you discover a vehicle defect that could make the vehicle unsafe to drive?

options.text: Drive slowly and report it at the end of the shift
Ignore it if the trip is short
Report it and do not operate the vehicle until it is confirmed safe
Ask another employee to drive it instead

questions.questionText: Road rage can be made worse by eye contact, gestures, retaliation, or aggressive driving.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: When driving at night, what does it mean to 'overdrive your headlights'?

options.text: Driving with high beams on too often
Driving faster than the distance your headlights allow you to see and stop safely
Driving with headlights on during daylight hours
Using headlights in rainy conditions

questions.questionText: A tire suddenly blows out while you are driving at highway speed. What is the safest initial response?

options.text: Slam on the brakes immediately
Grip the wheel firmly, maintain control, and slow gradually without sudden braking
Turn sharply toward the shoulder
Shut off the engine immediately

options.text: 29 CFR 1910.147 Lockout/Tagout
Section 5(a)(1), the General Duty Clause
29 CFR 1910.1200 Hazard Communication
29 CFR 1910.134 Respiratory Protection

2.questionText: True or False: Pre-trip safety activities such as adjusting mirrors and fastening a seat belt can be completed after the vehicle starts moving.

options.text: True
False

3.questionText: Which items should be included in a complete pre-drive vehicle check?

options.text: Tires only
Mirrors and lights only
Fuel level and personal items
Tires, mirrors, lights, and other safety-related items

4.questionText: Why do drivers maintain a space buffer or safety cushion around their vehicle at all times?

options.text: To comply with posted minimum following distance signs
To allow time to react and space to maneuver in an emergency
To prevent vehicles from passing in traffic
To reduce fuel consumption from wind drag

5.questionText: True or False: A heavier vehicle traveling at the same speed as a lighter vehicle requires more distance to stop safely.

options.text: True
False

6.questionText: A driver's eyes are fixed on a roadside billboard instead of the road ahead. Which type of distraction is this?

options.text: Manual distraction
Visual distraction
Cognitive distraction
Mechanical distraction

7.questionText: Why is texting while driving more dangerous than most other distractions?

options.text: It is only a visual distraction
It is only a manual distraction
It is only a cognitive distraction
It combines visual, manual, and cognitive distractions at the same time

8.questionText: A vehicle begins to hydroplane on a rain-covered highway. What is the correct immediate response?

options.text: Apply the brakes firmly to regain grip
Accelerate to push through the water layer
Release the accelerator gradually and avoid sudden steering or braking
Shift to a lower gear and turn sharply

9.questionText: True or False: Driving beside a large truck at the posted speed limit ensures you are in a safe position.

options.text: True
False

10.questionText: Another driver is following too closely behind your vehicle. What is the safest way to handle this?

options.text: Brake sharply to make them aware of the risk
Speed up to create more distance between vehicles
Gradually slow down and let the tailgating driver pass when it is safe
Make eye contact in your mirror to signal them to back off

11.questionText: After a minor crash in a company vehicle, what are the correct initial steps?

options.text: Drive away if the vehicle is still operable
Check for injuries, call police if needed, exchange information, document the scene, and notify a supervisor
Move all injured persons immediately regardless of possible spinal injuries
Wait and only report the crash if the other driver calls the police

12.questionText: During a pre-trip check, a driver notices a brake fluid leak under the company vehicle. What should they do?

options.text: Drive slowly and report it at the end of the shift
Ignore it if the trip is under five miles
Report the defect and not drive the vehicle until it is repaired and safe
Ask a coworker to drive the vehicle so the reporting obligation does not apply

13.questionText: True or False: Responding to an aggressive driver by making eye contact, gesturing, or retaliating can escalate a dangerous road rage situation.

options.text: True
False

14.questionText: A driver travels at 65 mph at night on an unlit road. The headlights only illuminate 200 feet ahead, but the stopping distance at this speed is 350 feet. This describes which dangerous condition?

options.text: Driving with high beams in an urban area
Overdriving headlights — traveling too fast to stop within the visible distance
Using improper headlights during daylight hours
Failure to use headlights in rain

15.questionText: A rear tire blows out at highway speed. Which initial action best keeps the vehicle under control?

options.text: Apply the brakes firmly to stop as quickly as possible
Grip the steering wheel firmly, maintain direction, and slow gradually without sudden braking
Steer sharply toward the shoulder lane
Shift to park and shut off the engine immediately
